latest.description:
🔗 jetzt auf Goetheanum.TV: https://goetheanum.tv/programs/im-klappern-der-schreibmaschine-selg

Peter Selg würdigt Helene Finckh (1883–1960), die brillante Stenografin Rudolf Steiners. Sie hielt rund ein Drittel seines Vortragswerks – etwa 1700 Vorträge – wortgetreu fest, übertrug sie in Reinschrift und bewahrte so spirituell zentrale Inhalte. Der Vortrag schildert ihren Weg von Stuttgart ans Goetheanum, geprägt von Verlusten und stiller Hingabe, und zeigt, wie ihre Arbeit das gesprochene Wort Steiners dauerhaft macht.

Ein Beitrag von Peter Selg zum Festakt zur Vollendung der Rudolf-Steiner-Gesamtausgabe.

In diesem Vortrag wird es um eine vertiefte Betrachtung von Rudolf Steiners sechs Nebenübungen gehen. Wenn wir diese Übungen vom Gesichtspunkt der Schwelle betrachten, wachen wir auf für ihren tieferen Sinn, der unmittelbar zu unserem Schicksalsfeld führt. Da wir heute alle an der Schwelle eines neuen Bewusstseins stehen, sind diese Übungen für uns alle gedacht!

Es ist ein inspirierender Abend mit Raum für Fragen und Austausch zu erwarten.

latest.title: Bernd Ruf: Emergency Pedagogy, Trauma, and Resilience | Wilton 2026
latest.description:
In a world shaped by collective trauma, school violence, and ongoing crises, what does it take to work with the most wounded among us without becoming wounded ourselves?                                                                  

Bernd Ruf, founder of the Parsifal Center in Karlsruhe and a pioneer of Waldorf emergency pedagogy, introduces the themes of Modules 5 and 11 of the Emergency Pedagogy training: severe targeted violence, the psychology of perpetrators, resilience research (Maslow, Antonovsky, Werner, Tedeschi), and the psycho-hygienic inner work that protects practitioners from secondary traumatization.

  He invites you to join him at the Center for Anthroposophy's Summer Weeks in Wilton, New Hampshire, in July 2026, where Modules 5 and 11 will be taught in person.
                                                                                                                          
Topics covered:
  • The rise of collective traumatization and why emergency pedagogy is more relevant than ever
  • What drives children to commit acts of targeted violence (Columbine, recent events)                                   
• Peter Langman's four-type perpetrator profile                                                                         • Trauma as a "contagious" condition and the need for psycho-hygienic protection                                        
• Resilience: individual factors, social networks, and a spiritual understanding of the human being                     
• How anthroposophy contributes to emergency pedagogical training                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                               
Originally recorded in German. English subtitles available (click CC).

latest.title: Искусство становящегося сообщества. Райнер Шнурре
latest.description:
Запись лекции состоялась 30 января 2019.
Москва, вальдорфская школа им. Пинского.
Переводчик Оксана Каплина.

Райнер Шнурре - антропософ из Германии, основатель направления "Художественная биографическая работа", "Искусство становящегося сообщества". На протяжении последних 5 лет Райнер приезжал из Германии и много времени проводил в России: вел образование, различные курсы и семинары, индивидуальные консультации. 

Райнер разработал художественную биографическую работу, построенную на феноменологическом подходе; всю жизнь занимался самовоспитанием и Socialkunstgeschaltung (Искусством становящегося сообщества). Много лет Райнер посвятил работе с зависимостями. Райнер Шнурре, как кинорежиссер, писатель и социальный художник, активно выступал за триединство социального организма. Для него была особенно важна встреча человека с человеком.

В 2021 году снял фильм «Накануне шторма» о социальной трехчленности (переведён на русский язык). Обучал динамическому рисованию знаков Зодиака по Вольфгангу Вегенеру, был его последним учеником. 

Последние 5 лет интенсивно работал в России с группами и возлагал большие надежды на Россию: «Только вы, русские, способны одушевить антропософию», говорил он в последнее время.
11 ноября 2023 года, через 14 дней после своего 78-летия, Райнер Шнурре перешёл Порог Духовного мира.

В России у него остались ученики, продолжающие и развивающие импульсы работы с духовным исследованием, биографией человека и с социальными вопросами. Каждый год в России проходят группы по динамическому рисованию Зодиака, художественной биографической работе и социальному вопросу. Переведены и выпущены на русский язык его книги и практические пособия по Художественной биографической работе, динамическому рисованию Зодиака, социальному искусству. В 2022 году вышла на русский язык его знаковая книга «Кармическое сообщество».

    We have just passed through the triad of festivals known as Halloween, All Souls, and All Saints. latest.description:
"In this video, we will show you the eurythmy gesture for the consonant D, as given by Rudolf Steiner.

 'Imagine a very beautiful, peaceful evening landscape. Not grandiose, but soft, gentle rolling hills. In the background, the sun is just setting between two hills. A few white clouds stand still, motionless in the sky, looking down upon a lovely meadow valley. A small stream flows by, murmuring quietly like a dream; trees and shrubs stand along its banks, reflecting in its still water; flowers bloom in the meadow, and on the slopes of the hills stand fruit trees full of ripening fruit. Perhaps, far off on one of the slopes, a person is still working quietly and peacefully, enveloped in this evening peace. Nature rests completely self-contained. And you walk through this valley, surrendered to and embraced by this peaceful mood, and with every single thing—be it a tree, the sun, the clouds in the sky, the flowers and shrubs of the meadow, the stream at your side, the person far away, the fruit of the orchard—you feel one and connected with everything, and you greet each one with this movement.' Then he made an unspeakably gentle, quietly lowering hand movement with the palm facing downward, several times in succession, repeatedly raising the relaxing hand and then lowering it again, stretched rather than strained down to the fingertips. It was like a leaf that had detached from its branch and, as if carried by the air, gently drifted down to the earth. 'That is a D. Learn to feel it as a reaction to a resting external influence. Practice it out of this mood, and with each "This through you" (Dies durch dich), turn your attention to a different thing in this external world. Even down to the feet, one should be gripped by the mood just described, and try to express it in the nature of one's step.'

This first description of the consonant D by Rudolf Steiner was written down by the first eurythmist, Lory Mayer-Smits."

latest.description:
¡Bienvenido a la finca bananera Granja Fátima en Santa Marta, Colombia!
Una hermosa experiencia de un "bosque de plátanos".
Visite esta granja biodinámica y certificada por Demeter en Colombia y siga a los agricultores Victoria y Louis que nos guían por ella. 
"Esto es una unidad. La granja Granja no es sólo lo que implican sus certificaciones, sino lo que es como unidad. Una granja como una granja: Nuestra Granja Fátima es preciosa. Vas caminando y te das cuenta de que estás en otro lugar. No es que te lo cuente, te invito a recorrerla. " - Victoria Bernier

Los plátanos son saludables, eso es bien sabido: la fruta perfecta y una fuente de vitaminas, minerales y fibra. Se consideran un alimento completo y son populares entre jóvenes y mayores.
Pero los plátanos también son una fruta problemática, precisamente por su popularidad. La demanda mundial conduce a un monocultivo, optimizado para la masa, que puede destruir ecosistemas enteros. Esto va acompañado de un uso masivo de productos químicos: la industria del plátano es un sector con un alto consumo de pesticidas. Esto tiene consecuencias devastadoras para el suelo, las aguas subterráneas y la biodiversidad. Sobre todo, para la salud de los trabajadores de las plantaciones, que a veces están expuestos a los productos químicos altamente tóxicos sin protección.
Los plátanos Demeter son diferentes de todos los demás plátanos del mercado, porque representan más de lo que puede ofrecer la palabra "ecológico". Se cultivan de acuerdo con las normas ecológicas más estrictas. No están optimizados para maximizar los beneficios y se cultivan sistemáticamente sin pesticidas ni contaminantes artificiales. Además, son el producto de los valores de los productores Demeter que piensan y actúan con amor, fuerza, alegría y libertad. Demeter practica una agricultura holística.

Who previous, were sleeping in the dark

Rules all beings living in the darkness
Rules the dark by telling countless lies

By spinning golden worlds of falsehoods
That feed within the soul the urge to fight

Liar Bird thinks that he is winning

Her gaze turned to the heights of heaven

Soph inspires the Holy Spirit’s mission
To bring the light of Truth down from above

All weary souls who hope and yearn for truth,

Ils apprennent en imitant les adultes qui cuisinent, rangent ou jardinent. Ils apprennent en jouant librement, en grimpant, en construisant, en explorant la nature. Ils apprennent en écoutant des histoires, en chantant, en vivant au rythme de journées prévisibles et rassurantes.

Dans les jardins d'enfants Waldorf, ces expériences ne sont pas une pause dans les apprentissages : elles en sont le fondement. L'autonomie naît des gestes du quotidien. Le langage se nourrit des échanges et des récits. La motricité se construit dans le mouvement libre. L'attention, la créativité, la confiance en soi et les compétences sociales se développent à travers le jeu et la vie partagée.

Ces apprentissages informels, profondément adaptés aux besoins du jeune enfant, préparent les acquisitions plus formelles qui viendront plus tard. Avant d'apprendre à lire, écrire ou compter, l'enfant construit les bases qui lui permettront de le faire avec confiance et enthousiasme.

Cathars of the Languedoc. Through glimpses from a study-tour to the Pyrenees and a Concert with Eurythmy. By Carol Holmsen.

Zoom talk with PowerPoint about the Troubadours and Cathars of the medieval Languedoc with illustrations, pictures and musical clips. Facts and romanticized fiction. This presentation is seen through the “lens” of a Concert with Eurythmy of Troubadour Music with a section on their neighbors and contemporaries, the Cathars, as well as through glimpses from a study-tour to the Pyrenees with Roland van Vliet in 2015. The 1987 series of Concerts with Eurythmy about the Troubadours and Cathars in Languedoc in the 1200’s was held in Norway. In the first part of this presentation, an attempt will be made to take a deep dive through immersion into the poetry and music of the Troubadours and the framework of ideas behind them. In the second part of this presentation, the story of the Cathars, who they were, what they believed, how they lived and their tragic end will be presented. 

Carol Holmsen has worked in the teaching and health fields and has a background in eurythmy, curative eurythmy, nursing, rhythmical massage, homeopathy, English and literature. Author, translator, sheep-keeper of Old Norwegian short-tailed sheep, and a weaver.

Troubadours and Cathars of the Languedoc. Through glimpses from a study-tour to the Pyrenees and a Concert with Eurythmy. Part 1: The Troubadours by Carol Holmsen.

Zoom talk with PowerPoint about the Troubadours and Cathars of the medieval Languedoc with illustrations, pictures and musical clips. Facts and romanticized fiction. Why a presentation about the troubadours and the Cathars in a webinar series about Manichaeism? Who were the Troubadours and the Cathars? What was Courtly Love? Examples of several Troubadour songs. What were Cathar beliefs? Were they connected with Manichaeism? What was the Albigensian Crusade which led to the demise of the Cathars and the decline of the Troubadours? 

This presentation is seen through the “lens” of a Concert with Eurythmy of Troubadour Music with a section on their neighbors and contemporaries, the Cathars, as well as through glimpses from a study-tour to the Pyrenees with Roland van Vliet in 2015. The 1987 series of Concerts with Eurythmy about the Troubadours and Cathars in Languedoc in the 1200’s was held in Norway. In the first part of this presentation, an attempt will be made to take a deep dive through immersion into the poetry and music of the Troubadours and the framework of ideas behind them. In the second part of this presentation, the story of the Cathars, who they were, what they believed, how they lived and their tragic end will be presented. 

Carol Holmsen has worked in the teaching and health fields and has a background in eurythmy, curative eurythmy, nursing, rhythmical massage, homeopathy, English and literature. Author, translator, sheep-keeper of Old Norwegian short-tailed sheep, and a weaver.

Vortrag von Tony Peleman im Rahmen der Festlichen Treffen zur Michaelizeit und zu seiner Schule – 24. Oktober 2026, online.

Thema des Abends: „Mut vor der Schwelle in der modernen Welt: der Weg der Schule Michaels anhand der 19 Lektionen der Ersten Klasse“.

The Mystery of Evil & incarnation of Ariman. A Michaelic Response to the great Challenge of our time. Part II. By Florian Sydow.

Drawing on Rudolf Steiner’s indications about the imminent physical incarnation of Ahriman, Florian Sydow will explore the mystery of evil as a decisive challenge of our time.  Working with the Sculptural The Representative of Humanity as a guiding image, we will consider the long-prepared conditions that enable Ahrimanic influence: materialism, the hardening of thinking, technological abstraction, and the erosion of truth.

At the heart of the talk is the battle within human intelligence, contrasting cold calculated Ahrimanic intelligence with heart-warmed Michaelic, morally enlivened thinking. In the context of artificial intelligence, transhumanism, and emerging super-intelligence, the focus will be on a Michaelic response: awakening to Christ’s Second Coming in the Etheric, cultivating a conscious relationship to Michael as Time-Spirit, and the spiritualization of intelligence through inner freedom.


Humanity’s collective crossing of the threshold calls for discernment and courage—so that evil is neither denied nor surrendered to, but consciously transformed in service of human evolution and the Earth’s destiny as a future Planet of Love.

Kunstwerke
„Wir modernen Menschen müssen Kunstwerke schaffen, bei denen die Form mehr sagt als die Natur sagt, aber ganz natürlich spricht, sodass jede einzelne Linie, jede einzelne Farbe wie ein Naturgebet wird für das Göttliche. ... Eigentlich möchte jede Pflanze, jeder Baum in einem Gebet aufblicken zum Göttlichen. ... Holen wir heraus, was in Baum und Pflanze, in Wolke und Stein an Linienführung an Farbe, an innerer Lebendigkeit lebt, prägen wir es de Bildhauermaterial ein, dann spricht durch das Kunstwerk die Natur zu den Göttern. Wir entdecken den Logos in der Natur. Und uns erscheint in unserer Kunst eine höhere Natur als die Natur draußen, eine Natur, die nun ihrerseits auf ganz natürliche Weise den Logos hinaufströmen lässt zu der göttlich-geistigen Welt.“, Rudolf Steiner, GA257

„..das siebente Siegel ist das von dem «Mysterium des Gral»,..  ein Würfel, die Raumeswelt darstellend, daraus von allen Seiten des Würfels entspringend die Weltenschlange, insofern sie die im niederen sich auslebenden höheren Kräfte darstellt; aus dem Munde der Schlange die Weltenlinie .. das Sinnbild der gereinigten und geläuterten Weltenkräfte; und daraus entspringend, der «heilige Gral», dem die «Taube» gegenübersteht:. hinweisend .. auf das Geheimnis der Weltzeugung, von der die irdische ein niederer Abglanz ist. Inneres Gleichgewicht - innere Harmonie
Übung für den 6. Monat

Ein inneres Gleichgewicht bildet sich durch die vorhergehenden/anderen Eigenschaften und Übungen ganz von selbst heraus. Durch Ausdauerndes, abwechselndes üben, der vorhergehenden Eigenschaften bildet sich allmählich ein schönes Gleichgewicht in der Seele. Man wird namentlich bemerken, dass etwa vorhandene Unzufriedenheit mit Erscheinungen und Wesen der Welt vollständig verschwinden.

Rudolf Steiner, GA10, GA12, GA95,S.117, GA 266a,S.238
    
Nebenübungen
Werden die höheren Wahrnehmungsorgane ausgebildet dies geschieht durch deiejenigen Kräften im Astralleib die während des Schlafes üblicherweise die verbrauchten Kräfte des physischen und ätherischen Leibes ersetzen. Diese Kräfte die zur Überwindung der Ermüdung der beiden unteren Leiber verwendet werden, sind es aber auch die die höheren Wahrnehmungsorgane ausbilden.
Wer seine esoterische Entwicklung beginnt, entzieht also dadurch eigentlich dem physischen und ätherischen Leib Kräfte. Diese sollten durch etwas anderes ersetzt werden. Hier gilt die allgemeine Weltenregel und okkulter Grundsatz: Rhythmus ersetzt Kraft!  Deshalb muss der Mensch daran arbeiten, dass Rhythmus in sein Leben hineinkommt. Gewisse Tätigkeiten muss er nach Möglichkeit regelmäßig ausführen. z. B. sollte jeden Morgen eine Meditations- und Konzentrationsübung zu einer bestimmten festgesetzten Zeit verrichtet werden, Abends eine Rückschau der Erlebnisse des Tages durchführen. Es entsteht so auch ein innerer Rhythmus, eine innere Harmonie. Physischer und ätherischer Leib werden nach und nach in solche Schwingungen versetzt, dass sie sich beim Heraustreten des Astralleibes selbst korrigieren können. (siehe Rudolf Steiner, GA10)

latest.title: Weekly Rhythms for the Waldorf Classroom: Let the Week Do Some of the Teaching
latest.description:
One of the greatest gifts of Waldorf education is rhythm.

When we think about rhythm, we often think first about the daily rhythm of the classroom or the larger rhythm of the school year. But one of the rhythms that has made the biggest difference in my own teaching is the rhythm of the week.

In this episode, I explore how giving each day its own character can simplify planning, reduce decision fatigue, and create a classroom that feels more grounded for both teacher and students.

I also introduce the idea of the planetary qualities associated with each day of the week—not as something to follow rigidly, but as an invitation to observe, experiment, and discover what resonates in your own classroom.

In this episode

🛎️ Why rhythm reduces planning fatigue 
🛎️ The difference between relying on engagement and relying on rhythm 
🛎️ The traditional planetary qualities of each weekday

latest.title: Authority and Waldorf Education
latest.description:
When I began teaching, I thought authority was something to avoid.

I wanted to be kind. Understanding. Flexible. I also lacked confidence and didn't feel particularly qualified to tell them what to do. I thought that if I cared enough, authority would somehow take care of itself.

It didn't.

Over time, I learned that children aren't looking for adults who step back—they're looking for adults who can step forward with calm confidence.

In this episode, I explore what authority really means in Waldorf education and why it has nothing to do with being authoritarian. Instead, authority is about holding a child's best interests at heart while providing the direction and certainty they cannot yet provide for themselves.

We discuss:

Why authority has become such an uncomfortable word
The difference between authority and authoritarianism
How children gradually develop inner authority
Why too many choices can sometimes increase a child's anxiety
Practical ways teachers can cultivate quiet authority in the classroom
Simple ways parents can practice loving authority at home
Why children "borrow" our authority before they can grow their own
Whether you're a classroom teacher or a parent, this episode is an invitation to rethink authority—not as control, but as one of the greatest gifts we can offer children as they grow toward freedom.

latest.title: A Day in Our Waldorf Kindergarten
latest.description:
In our Waldorf Kindergarten, the day unfolds gently through rhythm, warmth, and meaningful activity. Children arrive and settle into the space with care, placing their shoes and bags in their places and joining friends for fruit preparation. This simple act of cutting fruit together builds community and responsibility.

The morning begins with Circle Time, filled with songs, verses, and joyful movement that awaken the body and spirit. 

After sharing fruit together, the children step outdoors for free play — digging in the sand, exploring nature, and engaging in imaginative play.

Back in the classroom, the day continues with creative and hands-on activities such as beeswax modeling, wet-on-wet watercolor painting, cooking, and practical work. These experiences nurture creativity, patience, and a deep connection to the world around them.

There is also time for free indoor play, where imagination leads the way and simple materials transform into endless possibilities.

The day gently closes with story time and a goodbye circle, sending the children home held by rhythm, stories, and a sense of belonging.

In Waldorf education, every moment of the day is thoughtfully woven to nourish the child’s hands, heart, and head.

So yes, while Waldorf schools prioritize the exercise of handwriting, art, and bringing a page to life for the many cognitive and developmental benefits, we also practice it to nurture the soul of our holistic learning.

latest.title: Arts Integration in Waldorf Education
latest.description:
Art finds its way into all that we do - it is not an extra. Through the arts, subject matter comes to life through experience, creativity, and meaningful connection. As they study history, for example, students are invited not only to study facts about a period in time, but to enter into it through their own hands and imagination. 

Moreover, each project supports our curriculum in meeting our students where they are developmentally. For example, in 6th grade, at a time when their developmental stage seeks structure, order, and clarity, this work in calligraphy requires patience, deep focus, and adherence to form. latest.title: Perth Waldorf School Winter Festival 2026
latest.description:
To the Perth Waldorf School Community 

Thank You!

It was the perfect winter’s evening- still and crisp, with the stars lighting up the night sky. Over a thousand candles glowed around the grounds, the spirals almost hummed with energy, the bonfire stood ready to be lit. 

Everything was in readiness for children, parents and staff to play their part; like stepping on to the stage of ‘A Midwinter's Dream’.
 
And as a community, we did so with gentle reverence and beauty. We really know how to slow down to celebrate the inner experience that mid-winter brings: a rare thing in the hectic pace of life in this day and age.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The night began with Bruce and Sunu warmly welcoming each community member at the front gate.

The theme this year was the inner fire. 

On the Primary lantern walk three eurythmists – Sonia McGillivray, Rosemary Stevens and Romi Moreno and three speakers – Julia Humphreys, Jenny Hill and Sarah Boyle- spoke and moved parts of the Fire Blessing which had been gifted by aboriginal elder, Burnum Burnum. The three stations brought a sense of beauty and depth. The fire blessing was spoken again by the children before the lighting of the bonfire.

A highlight, as it has been for the past 3 years, was the Welcome to Country by Jayden Boundry and the traditional Noongar dancing. Hearing the didge and singing, seeing the dancers around the fire is always a special, powerful experience  and we highly value the ongoing relationship we have with them. 

Music

Claire Williamson led the Winter choir and parent singing and also prepared the Class 12s for their spectacular fire entrance. Michelle Guffie and Judith Schipkie worked with Claire to choreograph and rehearse movement for the Class 7s and 12s for their powerful fire lighting ceremony. Jenny Cowley and Yesim Atila taught songs in the Primary school. Yesim and Claire co-led the singing at the bonfire.

latest.title: AI當道，人心何價？華德福孩子如何在AI時代領航
latest.description:
講者陳志邦教授（Dominic Chan）是一位大學商科學院教授及華德學校家長，今次以「人工智能如何影響教育」為主題發表演講。

第一部份，他從經濟角度講解「年齡收入曲線（age-earning profile）」，指出以往社會相信人應該早年儲備知識、中年發揮、晚年退休，但AI打破了這種線性增長模式——AI無年齡限制、學習極快，年輕人與長者都可能被取代，傳統教育設計因此需要重新思考。

第二部份，他引用聖經中「大衛與歌利亞」的故事，說明人類不應盲目模仿巨人（主流、AI、制度），而應尋找自身獨特的優勢去面對挑戰。真正的關鍵不是「打贏AI」，而是「不需要與AI打一樣的仗」。

第三部份，他進一步引入「7C 未來能力架構」作為回應之道。這些能力正是AI難以模仿的「人性能力」，亦應該是教育的真正核心。

latest.title: Theosophy - Episode #4 - PODCAST
latest.description:
Welcome to Chapter #4 of Anthroposophy on Podcast! In today’s episode, we’ll be diving into Rudolf Steiner’s profound work Theosophy, where he explores the nature of human consciousness and the universe through the lens of spiritual science.

Steiner introduces us to the idea that we, as human beings, are far more than just physical bodies. He describes a complex spiritual constitution, made up of the ether body, the soul body, and the spirit self. These layers reveal how we exist not only in the material world but are deeply rooted in a spiritual reality.

In this chapter, we’ll explore how Steiner explains the physical world as a mere reflection of a deeper, spiritual realm. He describes how archetypes that exist in spiritland eventually manifest as physical forms, showing us the profound connection between the two worlds. Steiner emphasizes that by shifting our perception and embracing the interconnectedness of all things, we can access these spiritual dimensions through inner development.

Whether you’re new to these concepts or continuing your journey through Steiner’s teachings, this episode offers a deep exploration of the spiritual constitution and the transformative power of supersensible knowledge. Join us as we unravel the mysteries of Theosophy and its vision of the spiritual world.

She holds a Diploma in Horticulture.

latest.title: Work-based Training
latest.description:
The Biodynamic Agricultural College’s work-based training teaches a holistic, ecological approach to growing food and nurturing the land and people. You’ll learn practical skills working on some of the most incredible working farms in the UK while also developing a deeper understanding of how to produce high-quality food in cooperation with nature.

The training is designed along the lines of a classic apprenticeship, allowing you to earn while you learn. Working alongside experienced farmers and growers, you’ll gain the practical skills and confidence needed to run an agricultural enterprise. You’ll also take part in periodic seminars, bringing together students from across the UK to explore biodynamic principles, learn from over 30 teachers on a wide range of topics and reflect on how to apply what you’ve learned.

With more than 20 years of experience in the provision of agricultural education, we offer the most established professional training in sustainable farming in the UK and the only certified level 3 diploma in the agroecology sector.

Learn more: https://bdacollege.org.uk/we-have-two-trainings-which-will-suit-you/work-based-learning-course/biodynamic-work-based-diploma/

latest.title: Geburtshilfe als Balanceakt zwischen Hightechmedizin und natürlicher Geburt
latest.description:
Individuell, einzigartig, nicht planbar - so lässt sich jeder Beginn eines Lebensweges gut beschreiben. Jede Familie, jede Frau bringt ihre Sorgen, Erwartungen und Überzeugungen mit in den Kreißsaal. Die Wünsche der Frauen liegen zwischen unbegleiteter natürlicher Geburt und geplantem Kaiserschnitt. In diesem Spannungsfeld arbeitet die Geburtshilfe heute. Was macht das mit den Frauen und Kinder, aber auch mit den Ärzt:innen und Hebammen?

In der Lunch Session „Geburtshilfe als Balanceakt – zwischen Hightechmedizin und natürlicher Geburt“ am 21. Januar 2025 machten Prof. Dr. Michael Abou-Dakn (Facharzt für Frauenheilkunde und Geburtshilfe), Julia Grebner (Hebamme) und Dr. med. Jan Vagedes (Facharzt für Kinder- und Jugendmedizin, Neonatologe) unter der Moderation von Dr. med. Gabriela Stammer (Fachärztin für Frauenheilkunde und Geburtshilfe) ganz deutlich, dass es in der Geburtshilfe wieder viel mehr um Vertrauen, Geduld und Beziehung gehen muss - sei es unter der Geburt, im Umgang mit den Kolleginnen und Kollegen oder in der gezielten Förderung von Frühchen.

latest.title: Fieber - Freund oder Feind? Neues aus Forschung und Praxis
latest.description:
Zeigt das Thermometer mehr als 38,5 °C Körpertemperatur an, wird in der Medizin von Fieber gesprochen. Längst wissen Medizin und Forschung, dass das Fieber selbst keine Krankheit ist, sondern eine Reaktion des Körpers, um Infektionen bzw. die Erreger zu bekämpfen. Ein Kind mit Fieber kann sich besser gegen eine Erkrankung schützen, da das Fieber die Immunabwehr gegen Bakterien verbessert. Das Fieber selbst ist also nicht gefährlich, die zugrunde liegende Krankheit könnte es aber sein. 

Wie kann es gelingen, Eltern (und auch Ärztinnen und Ärzten) die Verunsicherung zu nehmen? Welchen Stellenwert nimmt dabei die 2020 entwickelte FeverApp ein? Wie sinnvoll sind fiebersenkende Mittel? Was tun, wenn es dem Kind sehr schlecht geht oder es unter Fieberkrämpfen leidet?

Diese und andere Fragen diskutierten Univ.- Prof. Dr. med. David Martin und Georg Soldner unter der Moderation von Dr. med. Stefan Schmidt-Troschke in der Lunch Session „Fieber – Freund oder Feind?“ am 3. Dezember 2024. 

Diese Session ist Teil der Serie "Anthroposophische Medizin im Dialog".

latest.title: Welchen Beitrag leistet das Konzept von `Early Palliative Care´ in der Onkologie?
latest.description:
Eine Krebsdiagnose ist immer ein Schock. Zwar kann Krebs in einem frühen Stadium immer besser behandelt werden, aber noch gewinnt nicht jeder den Kampf gegen diese Erkrankung. 
Was tun, wenn sich abzeichnet, dass eine Heilung nicht mehr möglich ist? Was macht das mit Betroffenen und ihren Angehörigen? Und wie können Patientinnen und Patienten in der Situation schon sehr früh gut begleitet werden? Dieser Frage stellt sich das Konzept der "Early Palliative Care". 

In der Lunch Session "Was leistet das Konzept der ´Eary Palliative Care´ in der Onkologie?" am 19. November stellten PD Dr. med. Petra Voiß (Direktorin der Klinik für Integrative Onkologie & Supportmedizin an den Evang. Kliniken Essen-Mitte) und Dr. med. Christian Grah (Leitender Arzt des Lungenkrebszentrums am Gemeinschaftskrankenhaus Havelhöhe in Berlin) ihre Ansätze zu dem Thema vor und erläutern wichtige Erkenntnisse aus Forschung und Praxis. 
Unter der Moderation von Philipp Busche (Ärztlicher Leiter an der Klinik Arlesheim) zeigten die Expert:innen, wie integrative Ansätze der Palliativversorgung bereits früh in der onkologischen Therapie eingesetzt werden können.

The Three Kings Preparation is one of a whole group of preparations created by Hugo Erbe (1885-1965) as a result of his lifelong work as a biodynamic farmer in Germany. He experienced a very close connection to the elemental world and sought ways of encouraging their beneficial influences.

The precious gifts brought by the three kings from the East were: Gold, symbol for worldly wisdom, Frankincense, devotional offering to the Gods and Myrrh, symbol for the victory of life over death.

Ancient mystery wisdom has always held these three substances as symbols of awareness for the spiritual events taking place behind the outer physical phenomena. When prepared in the right way these three holy substances can also serve as gifts to the earth and to the elemental world.

latest.title: Spreading BD Preparations on a Large Field
latest.description:
Each Spring and Fall we spread BD500 and BC (Biodynamic Compound Preparation or Barrel Compost) on our large hayfields. We stir and spread by hand. (See our “Stirring Large Quantities” video.) This video shows how we gather friends to walk the fields and spread the preparations.

Remember that the biodynamic preparations work energetically, so you don’t need to get them on every square foot. Rather, when the drops hit the ground they radiate out from their point of contact impacting the soil and plants. 

Some people wonder whether these two preparations are effective if they are not spread directly on bare soil. We have been spreading them on our fields for over twenty years and see great results. Some of the preparation does hit the soil between the plants and that seems to be enough. It is important to spread droplets in a flinging motion on a relatively windless day. 

If we don’t get to a field in the early spring before the grass gets too long, then we will spread BD500 and BC right after taking a first cut of hay. In the fall we spread after taking a second cutting of hay or after pasturing the fields.

For more information and to purchase the biodynamic preparations please visit our website: biodynamicsolutions.org.

Modern life often leaves us overstimulated and under-rested. Caffeine, constant information, blue-light exposure from screens, emotional pressures, and demanding daily environments all keep our nervous system active long after the day is done.

If you find yourself awake at night, gently bring your attention to a single word. Just one word. Hold it quietly in your awareness and return to it whenever your thoughts begin to wander.

When I first began this practice, the word I focused on was simply “word.”

This may sound surprisingly simple, yet with patience and persistence, it can help train the mind to quieten and allow natural sleep to return.

latest.title: The Question: What Weaves Between Us As Americans?
latest.description:
As he traveled through pioneer communities during the 1830s, Alexis de Tocqueville marveled at the natural tendency to community-building that lives in Americans, writing that volunteer associations are "the true mother science" of all healthy societies of the future. How alive is this tendency today? In the following series we will draw on our history we will meet some of the "Visionaries" who helped fashion community impulses--Benjamin Franklin, Booker T. Washington, Jane Addams, Lillian Wald--and those who in their work demonstrated four of the pillars on which a healthy community must stand--Roger Williams and the founding of Rhode Island, John Adams' defense of the British Soldiers in 1770, Jacob Riis' shining of light on the misery of life in the Lower East Side, and the students who through their sit-ins in Nashville strove to build the "Beloved Community."
Karl Fredrickson is the author of Stories From The American Journey: Men and Women Whose Lives and Deeds Express the Ideals of a Nation.

latest.title: Jacob Riis and Lillian Wald
latest.description: In the work of Jacob Riis in the tenements of 1880s Manhattan we have another of those "pillars" on which healthy communities rest: the awakening of others to the poverty and inequality faced by the less fortunate. With Lillian Wald and her "rooftop nurses" we have another of those "Community Visionaries."
